mainTopic: Whether חכמים can actively uproot Torah law, and the penalties on a woman who remarried in error
overview: Right before this, רבה taught that חכמים can uproot a Torah law when they only tell a person to sit back and not act (שב ואל תעשה). רב חסדא lists cases he had planned to challenge him from, then drops the challenge, because every one of them only involves not acting. The גמרא then tries to prove that a Torah law can also be uprooted by active doing. It brings three sources: a נביא like אליהו at הר הכרמל, a canceled גט, and בית דין punishing beyond Torah law. Each proof is pushed off. A נביא's power comes from a פסוק, and emergency steps to guard the Torah (מיגדר מילתא) are a special case. For the גט, every marriage rests on the approval of the רבנן, so they can cancel the קידושין, even קידושין made through ביאה. Then the גמרא goes back to the משנה about a woman who remarried in error. It explains why neither husband may become טמא for her, take her found objects or earnings, or cancel her vows. Finally it quotes the next line of the משנה: a בת ישראל in this case can no longer marry a כהן.

steps.title: רב חסדא's list of cases he planned to challenge from
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא tells רבה he wanted to challenge him from seven cases where a rabbinic rule stops a person from doing a Torah מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I wanted to challenge you from these cases: an uncircumcised man, sprinkling, the circumcision knife, a linen cloak with ציצית, the lambs of עצרת, שופר, and לולב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא lists, very briefly, cases he had planned to use against רבה. This sets up his next line, where he explains why he is not pressing the challenge after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In every case on the list, a rabbinic rule ends up keeping a person from a Torah מצוה, such as eating the קרבן פסח, wearing ציצית, blowing שופר, or taking לולב. That looks like חכמים uprooting Torah law, which seems to cut against רבה's point. The cases are given as one-word labels, so the learner has to know each one from elsewhere.

keyTerms.meaning: I wanted to challenge you
an uncircumcised man (here, one who cannot eat the קרבן פסח)
sprinkling of the purifying water on someone who is טמא מת
the knife used for a ברית מילה
a linen cloak with woolen ציצית
the lambs offered on שבועות

steps.confusionAlert: רב חסדא never actually asks this question. He is saying he WOULD have asked it, and in the next line he explains why he no longer will.

phrases.english: He said to him: I wanted to challenge you
phrases.notes: This is רב חסדא speaking to רבה.

phrases.english: from an uncircumcised man, and from sprinkling.
phrases.notes: Both cases involve rabbinic rules that keep someone from eating the קרבן פסח.

phrases.english: And from the circumcision knife, and a linen cloak with ציצית.
And from the lambs of עצרת, and the שופר, and the לולב.
phrases.notes: עצרת here means שבועות. The שופר and לולב cases are about when the day falls on שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבה's earlier teaching that חכמים may uproot Torah law through שב ואל תעשה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The limits of when חכמים may uproot a Torah law.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Many rabbinic rules block a Torah מצוה, which seems to show broad rabbinic power to uproot Torah law.

steps.title: All the cases count as sitting back, so there is no challenge
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא takes back his challenge: since רבה showed that שב ואל תעשה is not real uprooting, all seven cases fit that rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have taught us that 'sit and do nothing' is not uprooting, all of these are also cases of 'sit and do nothing.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא explains why he dropped his challenge. רבה's own principle already answers every case on the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each case, the rabbinic rule only tells a person not to act: don't eat, don't sprinkle, don't carry, don't attach ציצית, don't blow, don't take the לולב. It never requires an action that goes against the Torah. So all seven are שב ואל תעשה, which רבה already said does not count as true עקירה.

keyTerms.meaning: now that you have answered for us
sit and do nothing; holding back from an action
uprooting a Torah law
all of them

steps.whatToRemember: When חכמים tell us to hold back from doing a Torah מצוה, that is שב ואל תעשה and is not considered uprooting Torah law. All seven cases on רב חסדא's list fit this pattern.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the main rule of the סוגיא: rabbinic power to set aside Torah law works mainly through not acting, not through actively doing something the Torah forbids.

phrases.english: Now that you have answered for us
that 'sit and do nothing' is not uprooting,
all of these are also 'sit and do nothing.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the planned challenge from step 1 using רבה's own principle.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Puts all the cases into an already-accepted category (שב ואל תעשה).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The cases looked like חכמים actively uprooting Torah law.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each case is only holding back from action, so none is true עקירה.

steps.title: A נביא can tell you to break a Torah מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a source showing that a נביא may tell people to actively break a Torah law for a short time, like אליהו at הר הכרמל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: "To him you shall listen." This means that even if a נביא tells you to break one of the Torah's מצוות, as אליהו did at הר הכרמל, you must listen to him, as long as it is only for the need of that time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to challenge the idea that a Torah law cannot be uprooted by active doing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, all seven cases were שב ואל תעשה, where a person just sits back. Here a person actively breaks a Torah law because the נביא told him to, which is קום עשה. So it looks like a Torah law can be uprooted actively.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא is bringing a source as a proof or a challenge
To him you shall listen: the פסוק commanding us to obey a true נביא
A ruling for the need of the moment only, not a permanent change
Actively doing something, the opposite of שֵׁב וְאַל תַּעֲשֶׂה

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"To him you shall listen" —
even if he says to you:

phrases.aramaic: עֲבוֹר עַל אַחַת מִכׇּל מִצְוֹת שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה,
phrases.english: Transgress one of all the מצוות in the Torah,
for example, Eliyahu at Mount Carmel,
everything according to the need of the hour —
listen to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the שב ואל תעשה cases were settled, the גמרא looks for a case of active uprooting.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that a Torah law cannot be uprooted by actively doing something.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A נביא can tell people to actively break a Torah law, so active uprooting does exist.

steps.title: A נביא is different because the Torah commands us to obey him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a נביא is a special case, since a פסוק itself tells us to listen to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because it is written: "To him you shall listen."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof by saying the case of a נביא is special.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When we obey a נביא, the Torah itself gave that power through the פסוק "אליו תשמעון". So it is not a person uprooting the Torah. The Torah is allowing it, and that tells us nothing about the power of the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there: the case you brought is special
As it is written, pointing to a פסוק

phrases.english: It is different there,
as it is written: "To him you shall listen."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the נביא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: a פסוק gives the נביא this power.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A נביא's power shows that people can uproot Torah law actively.
steps.terutzMaskana: The נביא's power comes from a special פסוק, so we cannot learn from it about the רבנן.

steps.title: Let us learn the power of the רבנן from the נביא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we cannot learn from the נביא that the רבנן have the same power.
steps.simpleTranslation: So let us learn from it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: even if the נביא's power comes from a פסוק, we should be able to learn from it that the רבנן also have such power.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the Torah gave a נביא the power to set aside a law for the need of the time, it should work as a model. The רבנן should be able to do the same.

keyTerms.meaning: So let us learn from it, a request to treat one case as a model for another

phrases.english: So let us learn from it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the נביא is a special case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even a power that comes from a פסוק can serve as a model for the רבנן.

steps.title: Protecting the people's observance is a special case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that אליהו's act was to fence in the people's observance, which is a unique situation.
steps.simpleTranslation: Making a fence around a matter is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that we cannot learn a general rule from אליהו, because his act was an emergency step to protect the people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אליהו acted to pull the people away from עבודה זרה, which is a fence to strengthen observance. A special emergency step like that does not show that the רבנן can uproot a Torah law in ordinary cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Making a fence around a matter, an emergency step to strengthen observance

phrases.english: Making a fence around a matter is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the push-back in step 5 and closes the נביא proof.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: an emergency fence is an exception.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We could learn general power for the רבנן from אליהו.
steps.terutzMaskana: Emergency fencing is unique, so no general rule comes from it.
steps.whatToRemember: The נביא proof fails for two reasons: a פסוק gives the נביא his power, and אליהו's act was an emergency fence.

steps.title: The case of the canceled גט
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a dispute: רבי says a husband's cancellation of a גט works, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says it does not, because of the power of בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If the husband canceled the גט, it is canceled. These are the words of רבי. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: He cannot cancel it, and he cannot add to its condition. Because if so, what is the power of the בית דין worth?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to try again. This step quotes the source, and the next step will spell out the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן made a rule that a husband may not cancel a גט he already sent with a messenger. According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, if he cancels it anyway, the cancellation does not work, so that the בית דין's rule will have force.

keyTerms.meaning: He canceled it: the husband canceled the גט
It is canceled
Its condition, a condition written into the גט
What is the power of the בית דין worth? The rule of the בית דין must have force

phrases.english: Come and hear: If he canceled it — it is canceled,
phrases.notes: A husband who sent a גט with a messenger and then canceled it before a בית דין, even though the רבנן forbade this.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
He cannot cancel it,
nor add to its condition.

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן — מָה כֹּחַ בֵּית דִּין יָפֶה.
phrases.english: For if so — what is the power of the court worth?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the נביא proof was pushed off, the גמרא tries a new source.
steps.raayaObject: That the רבנן can actively uproot a Torah law.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The opinion of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל that the husband's cancellation does not work because of the power of בית דין.

steps.title: The רבנן let a married woman marry anyone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the challenge: by Torah law the גט is canceled, yet the רבנן treat her as divorced and let her marry anyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here, by Torah law the גט is canceled, and because of "what is the power of the בית דין worth" we permit a married woman to the whole world!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains why the canceled גט is a strong challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, the husband's cancellation works, so she is still an אשת איש. Yet the רבנן say the גט is valid, and she may marry another man. That is active uprooting of a Torah law, not just שב ואל תעשה.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law
A married woman
We permit
To the whole world, to marry any man

phrases.english: But here,
where by Torah law the bill of divorce is canceled,
and because of "what is the power of the court"
we permit a married woman to the whole world!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenge out of the source quoted in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the רבנן cannot actively uproot a Torah law.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רבנן actively permit a woman who is married by Torah law to marry anyone, which is uprooting by doing.
steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not just that the גט stays valid. It is that by Torah law she is still married, and the רבנן's rule lets her marry someone else.

steps.title: Every קידושין depends on the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a man makes קידושין on the authority of the רבנן, so the רבנן can cancel the קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever makes קידושין makes them on the authority of the רבנן, and here the רבנן took the קידושין away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining that the רבנן are not uprooting a Torah law here. Instead, they are canceling the marriage itself. The next step has רבינא pushing back on this answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every marriage is made on the condition that the רבנן agree to it. So when the רבנן keep the גט valid, they are really canceling the קידושין from the start, and she was never truly married. No Torah law is being broken.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes קידושין, betroths a woman
On the authority and approval of the רבנן
They took them away, canceled them

phrases.english: Whoever betroths — betroths on the authority of the Rabbis,
and the Rabbis canceled the betrothal,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the canceled גט.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing: the רבנן cancel the קידושין instead of overriding the Torah.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן are permitting a woman who is married by Torah law.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since קידושין rests on the רבנן's approval, they can take it away, so she is not an אשת איש.
steps.whyThisMatters: This idea, that every marriage rests on the approval of the רבנן, is a key tool the גמרא uses elsewhere to explain how the רבנן can affect marriage and divorce.

steps.title: What about קידושין done through relations?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב אשי: the answer that the רבנן can cancel קידושין works if he married her with money, but how does it work if he married her through ביאה?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: That works if he married her with money. But if he married her through relations, what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא pushes on the last answer. He asks how the רבנן can cancel קידושין that were not made with money at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With money, the רבנן can take the money away from him and make it ownerless, so no קידושין ever happened. But קידושין done through ביאה uses no money. There seems to be nothing for the רבנן to take away.

keyTerms.meaning: That works out fine (in one case), but...
He made קידושין with money
He made קידושין through marital relations
What is there to say? (How do you answer that?)

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
This works out well when he betrothed with money,
phrases.notes: With money, the רבנן can simply make the money ownerless, so the קידושין never took effect.

phrases.english: but if he betrothed through relations, what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתִינַח דְּקַדֵּישׁ בְּכַסְפָּא, קַדֵּישׁ בְּבִיאָה מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reach of the answer in Step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the רבנן can cancel any קידושין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Canceling by taking away the money only works when money was used. It does not explain קידושין done through ביאה.

steps.title: The רבנן made his relations count as בעילת זנות
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן declared that his ביאה is just בעילת זנות, not an act of קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן made his relations into relations of זנות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבינא. The רבנן can also cancel קידושין done through ביאה, because they declare that ביאה to be בעילת זנות and not קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every man makes קידושין on the authority of the רבנן. So the רבנן can decide that his ביאה never counted as קידושין. It becomes like an ordinary forbidden act that creates no marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן made it into / declared it to be
An act of relations
Relations outside of marriage, which create no קידושין

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן can cancel קידושין in both ways. With money, they take the money away. With ביאה, they declare it בעילת זנות.

phrases.english: The Sages made his relations into
licentious relations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's challenge in Step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extends the רבנן's power from money to ביאה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without money, the רבנן would have nothing to take away, so they could not cancel the קידושין.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן can declare the ביאה itself to be בעילת זנות, so the קידושין is canceled.

steps.title: בית דין may punish beyond Torah law: the horse rider
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן יעקב says בית דין may punish people even when the Torah does not, to protect the Torah. In the time of the Greeks, a man who rode a horse on שבת was stoned.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי אלעזר בן יעקב said, I heard that בית דין may give lashes and punish people even when the Torah does not call for it. This is not to break the Torah but to make a fence around it. There was a story about a man who rode a horse on שבת in the days of the Greeks. They brought him to בית דין and stoned him. This was not because he deserved it, but because the time needed it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source about the power of בית דין. Here בית דין actually did something, stoning a man, even though Torah law did not require it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Riding a horse on שבת is only forbidden by the רבנן. By Torah law it does not deserve stoning. Yet בית דין stoned the man. This shows that בית דין can actively go beyond the Torah's rules when the times demand it.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (a source is being brought)
They give lashes and punish
Not required by Torah law
A fence (protection) around the Torah
The time needed it (an emergency step)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think בית דין changed the הלכה of riding a horse into a סקילה sin. It stayed only a rabbinic איסור. The stoning was a one-time emergency step for that time.

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: Come and hear, Rabbi Elazar ben Ya'akov said:
I have heard that the court gives lashes and punishes
not by Torah law,
and not in order to transgress the words of the Torah,
but to make a safeguard for the Torah.
And there was an incident with a certain person
who rode on a horse on Shabbat
phrases.notes: Riding a horse on שבת is forbidden only by the רבנן, not by the Torah.

phrases.english: in the days of the Greeks —
and they brought him to the court and stoned him,
not because he deserved this,
but because the hour required it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source about בית דין's power to act against Torah law
steps.raayaObject: That בית דין can uproot Torah law even by actively doing something
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אלעזר בן יעקב's teaching and the story of the horse rider who was stoned

steps.title: A second story: the man under the fig tree
steps.stepSummary: A man was with his own wife in public under a fig tree. בית דין gave him lashes, because the time needed it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another story: a man was with his wife under a fig tree. They brought him to בית דין and gave him lashes. This was not because he deserved it, but because the time needed it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבי אלעזר בן יעקב's teaching with a second story. Here too, בית דין punished someone beyond Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah does not forbid a man to be with his own wife, even outdoors. Still, בית דין gave him lashes to stop public immodest behavior. The exclamation mark shows the proof is now complete: בית דין punishes with real actions, not only by holding back.

keyTerms.meaning: He was with his wife (had relations)
Under the fig tree, in a public place
They gave him lashes

phrases.english: And again, an incident with a certain person
who had relations with his wife under the fig tree,
phrases.notes: He did it out in the open where people could see, which is why it was a problem.

phrases.english: and they brought him to the court and flogged him.
Not because he deserved this,
but because the hour required it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and completes the proof begun in Step 12
steps.raayaObject: That בית דין can actively punish beyond Torah law
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the man under the fig tree who was given lashes

steps.title: Guarding the Torah is a special case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that making a fence for the Torah is different.
steps.simpleTranslation: Making a fence around something is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the proof aside. These stories only show what בית דין may do to protect the Torah in a time of need.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both stories were special steps to strengthen Torah observance, like אליהו on the mountain in Step 6. They do not teach that the רבנן can always uproot Torah law by an action. That power belongs to emergency fence-making.

keyTerms.meaning: Making a fence around a matter (protecting Torah observance)
Is different

steps.whatToRemember: Stories where בית דין acted beyond the Torah are special cases of guarding the Torah. They are not a general power to uproot Torah law.

phrases.english: Safeguarding a matter is different.
phrases.notes: This is the same answer given about אליהו in Step 6.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from Steps 12-13
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Limits the stories to emergency fence-making
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes these were normal uses of power, but they were special steps to protect Torah observance.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: neither husband may become טמא for her
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: neither the first husband nor the second may become טמא for this woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: Neither this one nor that one may become טמא for her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now leaves the discussion about the רבנן's power and goes back to the משנה. It quotes a new rule to explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If either husband is a כהן and the woman dies, neither may become טמא to bury her. A כהן normally may become טמא for his wife. Here, though, she is not treated as a proper wife to either man.

keyTerms.meaning: Neither this one nor that one (the first husband or the second)
Become טמא for her (a כהן at her death and burial)

phrases.english: Neither this one nor that one becomes impure for her.
phrases.notes: This is the woman from the משנה who remarried after hearing her first husband died, and then he came back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה and opens a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Neither husband, if a כהן, may become טמא for this woman.

steps.title: Where do we learn this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of this rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source. It is setting up the next step, which will bring a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants a Torah source showing which wife a כהן may become טמא for. That will explain why this woman does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: From where do we derive this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule in Step 15
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source that neither husband may become טמא for her

steps.title: The פסוק: "שארו" means his wife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts its answer with the פסוק that lets a כהן become טמא for "שארו," and explains that "שארו" means his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: "Only for his relative who is close to him." And the Master said: "His relative" means his wife,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer with a פסוק. It explains that the word "שארו" refers to a כהן's wife, so a כהן may become טמא for her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets up the base rule that a כהן may become טמא for his wife. The sentence is not finished yet. The next step explains why this woman does not count as "שארו" for either husband.

keyTerms.meaning: His relative, explained as his wife
The Master said (quoting an earlier teaching)

phrases.english: As it is written: "But for his relative, who is close to him,"
and the Master said:
"His relative" — this is his wife,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of Step 16
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is the פסוק about "שארו," which means a כהן's wife. Step 18 completes the derivation.

steps.title: A husband becomes impure for a fit wife but not for a disqualified one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a second פסוק that says a husband may NOT become טמא. It settles the clash between the two פסוקים by saying he becomes טמא for a fit wife but not for a disqualified wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written: 'A husband shall not become impure among his people, to profane himself.' So there is a husband who becomes impure, and there is a husband who does not become impure. How so? He becomes impure for his fit wife, but he does not become impure for his disqualified wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer from the last step. It sets a second פסוק next to the first and uses the two together to prove the rule of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One פסוק lets a כהן become טמא for his wife (שארו), and another says a husband may not become טמא. The גמרא solves this by splitting them: a כשרה wife, yes, and a פסולה wife, no. This woman is פסולה to both men, so neither may become טמא for her.

keyTerms.meaning: A husband shall not become impure
To profane himself, meaning to lower his כהונה status
How so? How do the two fit together?
Fit, a wife who is allowed to him
Disqualified, a wife who is forbidden to him

steps.whatToRemember: A כהן may become טמא only for a wife who is כשרה to him. The woman in our משנה is פסולה to both husbands, so neither may become טמא for her.

phrases.english: And it is written: "A husband shall not become impure among his people, to profane himself,"
there is a husband who becomes impure,
and there is a husband who does not become impure.
How so?
He becomes impure for his fit wife,
but he does not become impure for his disqualified wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְתִיב: לֹא יִטַּמָּא בַּעַל בְּעַמָּיו לְהֵחַלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in step 17 by adding the contrasting פסוק and resolving the two.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two פסוקים together teach that a husband becomes טמא for a fit wife but not for a disqualified one, so neither husband may become טמא for this woman.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: neither husband gets her found objects
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: neither husband is entitled to what she finds.
steps.simpleTranslation: And neither this one nor that one is entitled to her found objects, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה. It is setting up the explanation that comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a husband owns what his wife finds. The משנה says that in this case neither man gets it, and the גמרא will now explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one, meaning both husbands
Entitled to, have a right to
A found object

phrases.english: And neither this one nor that one
is entitled to her found objects, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה after finishing the טומאה rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Neither husband is entitled to the woman's found objects.

steps.title: Why she keeps her found objects: let him resent her
steps.stepSummary: The husband normally gets her found objects so he will not resent her. Here the רבנן do not mind if he resents her very much.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason the רבנן said a wife's found object belongs to her husband? So that he should not have resentment toward her. Here, let him have resentment upon resentment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the משנה's rule. It gives the normal reason a husband gets his wife's found objects, then shows that this reason does not apply here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that a wife's found object goes to her husband was made to keep peace and avoid איבה. In our case the רבנן want this marriage to end. So there is no reason to protect the peace, and the rule falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Resentment, ill will
So that ... should not

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying resentment is a good thing. It is saying the reason for the normal rule, keeping the peace, does not exist in a marriage the רבנן want to end.

phrases.english: What is the reason the רבנן said
that a wife's found object belongs to her husband?

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלָא תִּיהְוֵי לֵיהּ אֵיבָה.
phrases.english: So that he should not have resentment toward her.
Here, let him have resentment upon resentment.
phrases.notes: The רבנן want this couple to split up, so they don't mind if he resents her.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא מַאי אֲמוּר רַבָּנַן מְצִיאַת אִשָּׁה לְבַעְלָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the משנה line quoted in step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The found-object rule exists to prevent איבה. Here the רבנן do not care about איבה, so the rule does not apply.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: neither husband gets her earnings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next words of the משנה: neither husband is entitled to her earnings.
steps.simpleTranslation: And to her earnings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next item in the משנה. It is setting up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's list continues: neither man is entitled to her earnings either. The words 'neither husband is entitled' carry over from the line before.

keyTerms.meaning: Her earnings, literally 'the work of her hands'

phrases.english: And to her earnings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next item in the same list in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Neither husband is entitled to the woman's earnings.

steps.title: Why she keeps her earnings: she gets no food from him
steps.stepSummary: Earnings normally go to the husband because he feeds her. Here she has no right to food from him, so her earnings are not his.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason the רבנן said a wife's earnings belong to her husband? Because she eats his food. Here, since she has no right to food, her earnings are not his.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why neither husband gets her earnings. It uses the same pattern as before: here is the normal reason, and here is why it does not apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband gets his wife's מעשה ידיה as a trade for giving her מזונות. In this case she loses her right to מזונות, so the trade falls apart and he gets no earnings either.

keyTerms.meaning: Food, the husband's duty to support his wife
She does not have
Not his

phrases.english: What is the reason the רבנן said
that her earnings belong to her husband?
Because she eats his food.
Here, since she does not have food from him,
her earnings are not his.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא מַאי אָמְרִי רַבָּנַן מַעֲשֵׂה יָדֶיהָ לְבַעְלָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the משנה line quoted in step 21, following the same pattern as step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Earnings are a trade for food. Since she gets no food, he gets no earnings.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: neither husband cancels her vows
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: neither husband can cancel her vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he does not cancel her vows.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the last item of this list in the משנה. It is setting up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a husband can be מפר his wife's נדרים. The משנה says that here neither man has that power.

keyTerms.meaning: Cancels, annuls
Her vows

phrases.english: And he does not cancel her vows.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next item in the same list in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Neither husband may cancel the woman's vows.

steps.title: Why he cannot cancel her vows: let her become unattractive to him
steps.stepSummary: The Torah lets a husband cancel vows so his wife will not become unattractive to him. Here it does not matter if she becomes very unattractive to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason the Torah said a husband cancels vows? So that she should not become unattractive to him. Here, let her become very unattractive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the last rule with the same pattern. It gives the reason a husband can cancel vows and shows that the reason does not fit this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the source is the Torah itself (רחמנא), not the רבנן. The power to be מפר exists to keep her attractive to him. Since this marriage is meant to end, that goal no longer matters, so the power goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
She will become unattractive, repulsive to him

steps.whatToRemember: All three rules share one idea. Each marriage right exists for a reason (peace, support, or keeping her attractive to him). When the marriage must end and the reason does not apply, the right falls away.

phrases.english: What is the reason the Merciful One said
that a husband cancels her vows?
So that she should not become unattractive to him.
Here, let her become very unattractive.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא מַאי אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא בַּעַל מֵיפֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the משנה line quoted in step 23, completing the three-part pattern from steps 20 and 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The power to cancel vows exists so she will not become unattractive to him. Here that does not matter, so neither husband can cancel her vows.

steps.title: Quoting the next line: she is disqualified from marrying a כהן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next words of the משנה: if the woman was a בת ישראל, she becomes disqualified from marrying into כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה taught: if she was a בת ישראל, she becomes disqualified from marrying into the כהונה, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, which says a בת ישראל in this situation can no longer marry a כהן. This is a setup line, and the גמרא is getting ready to discuss it next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 19-24 dealt with found objects, earnings and vows between her and the two husbands. Now the משנה moves to a new kind of penalty, one about her personal status. She is no longer allowed to marry a כהן, so this changes who she may marry in the future.

keyTerms.meaning: A Jewish woman who is not from a family of כהנים or לויים
She became disqualified or unfit
The priesthood; here it means marrying a כהן
"Etc.": the quote goes on, but only its opening words are cited

phrases.english: If she was an Israelite woman
she is disqualified from the priesthood, etc.
phrases.notes: "From the priesthood" means she can no longer marry a כהן. The "etc." tells you the משנה keeps going, but the גמרא only quotes the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיְתָה בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל נִפְסְלָה מִן הַכְּהוּנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the line-by-line walk through the משנה. After finishing the vows line in steps 23-24, the גמרא quotes the next penalty, which is about her status.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בת ישראל who remarried based on false testimony that her husband died becomes disqualified from marrying into כהונה.
